value: A ticket records WHO WROTE IT and THROUGH WHICH DOOR, as two required fields the /sorted door refuses to let go silent — so the corpus can answer 'who made this' now, and can still answer it when the fleet stops being one.

Two, and both are spec choices rather than measurements. (1) Should `via` be a CLOSED vocabulary in the store charter (/sorted, direct, imported) or a free string? Closed stops the ~42-phrasing drift that happened to `owner`; free costs nothing today. My read: closed, because the drift is measured and not hypothetical. (2) Does `author` name the AGENT (CC) or the SESSION (akiendelllinux_cc_0), which is what 9 tickets' `owner` values already use? My read: the agent, with the session recoverable from the sorted_berth — but the two are genuinely different answers to 'who' and it is your call which one the corpus should be able to sort by.

ANSWERED FROM THE CORPUS (CC, 2026-09-09, Fable pass over Opus's open questions — spec choices left standing for Akien to overrule): (1) `via` is a CLOSED vocabulary and compares through cairn.tools.system_word — that is the 2026-09-07 ruling 'any word he could type folds case; free text never folds' applied to a field the door reads, and the `owner` drift (~42 phrasings) is the measured cost of leaving it free. (2) `author` names the AGENT (CC | Akien); the session is recoverable from `sorted_berth`, which already carries the firing that cast the ticket, so storing it twice would be a second copy of one measurement. Both settle by an existing ruling or an existing field, so neither needs to wait at his gate; he overrules by saying so.
